from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/lho-lho-nzr-aati-hai-karbala-ki-fza.md')
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True)
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1]
def words(s):
    return re.sub(r'"'^'"\\s*\\d+\\)?(?: +|"'$)'"', '', s, flags=re.M).lower().split()
assert words(old.split('---', 2)[2]) == words(roman)
for edition in (roman, body):
    assert [len(block.splitlines()) for block in edition.strip().split('\\n\\n')] == [2, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4]
print('Roman wording and matching verse counts verified')
PY"

from pathlib import Path
from textwrap import dedent
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/lho-lho-nzr-aati-hai-karbala-ki-fza.md')
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = dedent(meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1])
for edition, numerals in ((roman, '12345'), (body, '۱۲۳۴۵')):
    opening, *stanzas = edition.strip().split('\\n\\n')
    assert len(opening.splitlines()) == 2
    assert [s.splitlines()[0] for s in stanzas] == list(numerals)
    assert all(len(s.splitlines()) == 4 for s in stanzas)
assert all(line == line.rstrip() for line in p.read_text().splitlines())
print('Matching opening, five stanzas, and 17 verses verified')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed the Urdu script in [the selected lyric](src/data/lyrics/lho-lho-nzr-aati-hai-karbala-ki-fza.md) and moved the Roman wording into `romanLyrics`. I treated the opening as a preamble and joined wrapped phrases into single verse lines. Both editions contain 17 verses across the preamble and five stanzas.

I read the final “jhula rahi jhula” as “جھلا رہی جھولا.” The file now uses right-to-left direction and the `noUrdu` tag was removed.
